title: Stored XSS via unescaped job.display_class in _job_info.erb
analysis: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Sidekiq Web UI job details partial `web/views/_job_info.erb`. The template renders the `job.display_class` (which returns the class name of the job from the Redis payload) directly without HTML escaping (`<%= job.display_class %>`). Because Sidekiq permits any arbitrary string as the class name during job normalization and push (in `Sidekiq::JobUtil#normalize_item`), an attacker can submit a job with a malicious class name containing HTML or JavaScript (e.g., `">`). When an administrator views the job details page (e.g. for scheduled, retries, or dead jobs), the script will execute in the administrator's context. Conceptual Exploit Payload: Enqueue a job with a malicious class name via a Redis client, or through a custom client pushing to the queues: ```json { "class": "\">", "args": [], "queue": "default" } ``` When this job fails or is scheduled, and the administrator views the job info page at `/scheduled/[KEY]`, `/retries/[KEY]`, or `/morgue/[KEY]`, the browser will render: ```html "> ``` And trigger the JavaScript execution.

title: Stored XSS via unescaped queue and display_class in retries.erb
analysis:
A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Sidekiq Web UI retries list template `web/views/retries.erb`. The template renders both `entry.queue` and `entry.display_class` without HTML escaping (`<%= entry.queue %>` and `<%= entry.display_class %>`). Since any arbitrary string can be supplied as the queue name or class name in the job payload, an attacker can submit a job containing malicious HTML/JavaScript in either parameter. When the job fails and enters the retries set, and an administrator views the retries list at `/retries`, the injected scripts will execute in the administrator's browser.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Enqueue a job with a malicious class name:
```json
{
  "class": "\"><script>alert('class XSS')</script>",
  "args": [],
  "queue": "default"
}
```
Or with a malicious queue name:
```json
{
  "class": "MyJobClass",
  "args": [],
  "queue": "default\"><script>alert('queue XSS')</script>"
}
```
When this job fails and enters the retry set, viewing `/retries` will render the unescaped payloads and trigger the XSS.
snippet: <%= entry.queue %> <%= entry.display_class %> <%= display_tags(entry, "retries") %>

title: Stored XSS via unescaped job class name in metrics.erb
analysis: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Sidekiq Web UI metrics template `web/views/metrics.erb`. The template renders the job class name variable `kls` without HTML escaping inside several HTML elements, including `id="<%= id %>"`, `value="<%= kls %>"`, and the link `<%= kls %>`. If a job class name contains HTML/JavaScript (e.g. `">`), and its execution is successfully tracked and persisted in Redis, the malicious script will execute in the administrator's context when viewing the `/metrics` dashboard. Conceptual Exploit Payload: To trigger the metrics tracking, the job must execute successfully (since execution is required to record success/failure count and runtime metrics in the tracker). While standard Class name checks usually exist in the processor, if a custom adaptor or class loading stub permits the constant definition or mapping, or if the tracker is manually populated with arbitrary keys, the metric class name can contain HTML. When an administrator views the `/metrics` dashboard, the payload renders as: ```html " class="metrics-swatch" value="">" /> ?period="> ``` This triggers the stored XSS.
snippet: <% id = "metrics-swatch-#{kls}" %> /> <%= kls %>

title: Open Redirect via Referer Bypass in reload_page
analysis:
An open redirect vulnerability exists in Sidekiq::WebAction#reload_page. The method attempts to extract a safe local path from the HTTP Referer header by stripping `request.base_url` using `gsub`. However, if the attacker provides a Referer like `http://localhost:3000.attacker.com/foo`, the base URL `http://localhost:3000` is removed, leaving `.attacker.com/foo`. When this is passed to `redirect`, it prepends `request.base_url` again, resulting in `http://localhost:3000.attacker.com/foo`. This is a valid absolute URL pointing to the attacker's server, bypassing the redirection check.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Send a POST request to `/change_locale`:
```http
POST /change_locale HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
Referer: http://localhost:3000.attacker.com/foo
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

authenticity_token=[VALID_CSRF_TOKEN]&locale=en
```
Response:
```http
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: http://localhost:3000.attacker.com/foo
```
snippet:
def reload_page
      current_location = request.referer.gsub(request.base_url, "")
      redirect current_location
    end
